# Meghmani Organics Ltd (MOL.NS) — Quick Research Brief

**As of close, 9 Jul 2026 | Sector: Basic Materials — Agricultural Inputs | Currency: INR**

## Snapshot
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| Last price | ₹46.39 (+0.89% on the day) |
| Market cap | ~₹1,180 crore |
| Shares outstanding | ~25.4 crore |
| 52-week range | ₹36.50 – ₹106.30 |
| Drawdown from 52w high | ~56% |

$MOL is a small-cap agri-inputs / specialty chemicals player headquartered in Gujarat. The stock has had a punishing 12 months — down ~54% over the trailing 52 weeks and currently sitting in the lower third of its yearly range, not far off the ₹36.50 March 2026 low.

## Valuation — cheap on assets, expensive on earnings
| Ratio | Value | Read |
|---|---|---|
| P/E (TTM) | ~41.1x | Optically very expensive — but distorted by a near-collapse in earnings (see below) |
| P/B | ~0.75x | **Below book value**; book value per share ≈ ₹61.55 vs price ₹46.39 |
| P/S | ~0.54x | Trading at under 0.6x trailing revenue |
| EV/EBITDA | ~10.6x | Reasonable for a cyclical chemicals name once earnings normalise |
| EPS (TTM) | ₹1.13 | Thin; the high P/E is an artifact of depressed net income, not a rich price |
| Forward P/E | n/a | Not provided by the data feed |
| Dividend yield | **None reported** | No DPS / yield in the feed — MOL does not currently appear to be paying a regular dividend (see Dividends section) |

**The headline tension:** the stock is cheap on book and sales but optically dear on earnings. That gap is explained by the collapse in profitability over the last year.

## Profitability & Quality — deeply cyclical, currently in a trough
| Metric | Value |
|---|---|
| ROE | ~1.88% (TTM) |
| ROA | ~1.18% |
| Gross margin | ~39.0% |
| Operating margin | **−2.0%** (TTM, i.e. operating loss) |
| Net profit margin | ~1.3% |
| Revenue (TTM) | ~₹2,174 crore |
| Net income (TTM) | ~₹28.7 crore |
| Free cash flow (TTM) | ~₹95.0 crore (positive — a relative bright spot) |
| Debt / equity | ~0.47x (moderate) |
| Current ratio | ~1.07 (tight) |
| Quick ratio | ~0.57 (low — inventory-heavy working capital) |

Margins have inverted — the company is running at a **trailing operating loss** while still eking out a tiny net profit thanks to other income / finance-cost structure. ROE under 2% tells you the current earnings power is minimal. The positive trailing FCF (~₹95 cr) versus ~₹29 cr net income suggests depreciation-heavy capex accounting and/or working-capital release — worth checking in the cash-flow statement directly.

## Growth — both legs negative
| Metric | Value (MRQ YoY) |
|---|---|
| Revenue growth | **−14.3%** |
| Earnings growth | **−59.0%** |

This is the core fundamental problem: revenue is shrinking double-digit YoY and earnings have been more than halved. For an agri-inputs/specialty-chemicals name this reads like a cyclical downswing (likely pigment/chemical pricing and demand softness) rather than a structural break, but the trough is clearly deep.

## Dividends
- The data provider reports **no dividend per share and no dividend yield** for MOL (both `null` in fundamentals and derived fields). There is no evidence in the feed of a current regular cash dividend.
- **Honest caveat:** I could not pull a detailed historical dividend history from the structured feed, and the web search backend returned no results to corroborate a specific recent payout. Treat the "no dividend" reading as a data-feed signal, not a definitive statement — verify directly via the company's investor-relations page or the NSE/BSE corporate-action history before relying on it for an income thesis.

## Latest Quarter — Q4 FY2026 (announced 14 May 2026)
- MOL released its **Q4 FY26 financial results on 14 May 2026** [1], with a newspaper publication on 15 May [2] and an earnings call transcript filed on 19 May [3].
- The YoY MRQ growth figures above (revenue −14.3%, earnings −59.0%) are the most recent-quarter readings the fundamentals provider carries, and they align directionally with the weak full-year TTM picture. The earnings call transcript (Q4 FY26) is available on the NSE archives for a line-item breakdown [3].
- **I could not retrieve the granular Q4 line items (revenue/EBITDA/PAT/EPS) from the structured feed or corroborate them via web search** (the search backend returned zero results for the query, and web-search capacity was capped for this run). For exact quarterly numbers, open the press release PDF or transcript directly:
  - Press release (14 May 2026): [NSE PDF](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/MOL_14052026165235_PressRelease.pdf) [1]
  - Earnings call transcript (Q4 FY26): [NSE PDF](https://nsearchives.nseindia.com/corporate/MOL_19052026102404_TRANSCRIPT_Q4FY26.pdf) [3]

## Corporate-action context — ongoing restructuring (important)
Several recent NSE/BSE filings point to a **significant scheme of arrangement (likely a demerger/restructuring)** currently being executed through the NCLT route [4][5][6][7][8][9][10]:
- Court/NCLT-convened meetings of **equity shareholders, secured creditors, and unsecured creditors** were held on **6 June 2026**, with voting results and scrutinizer's reports filed on 9 June [4][5][6].
- The trading window was closed on 29 June 2026 ahead of the Q1 FY27 results window [11][12].
- A **SEBI takeover-regulation disclosure** was filed on 30 June 2026 [13], suggesting a possible change/clarification in promoter or substantial-shareholder holdings tied to the scheme.

**Read:** MOL is mid-restructuring. A demerger-type scheme that has cleared creditor and shareholder votes is a material catalyst — it can unlock value (the 0.75x P/B looks even cheaper if a separate entity holds valuable assets) but also creates near-term overhang and accounting noise. The 54% drawdown and the depressed margins are occurring *against this restructuring backdrop*, so the headline multiples are not a clean read on the operating business.

## Price action — 1-year daily
- The stock fell from the ₹50s in Feb 2026 to a **₹36.50 low on 30 Mar 2026**, then ripped to **₹61.50 on 6 May 2026** (on very heavy volume — ~29.7M shares on 5 May, vs typical 0.3–1.5M) — consistent with a positive restructuring/corporate-action catalyst.
- Since that May spike it has bled back to **₹46.39**, consolidating in a ₹45–53 range through June–early July. The stock is now ~25% off its May rebound high and ~56% off the 52-week high of ₹106.30.
- Beta is low (~0.56), so the drawdown is idiosyncratic / company-specific, not a market-beta artifact.

## Bear case vs. Bull case
| Bear | Bull |
|---|---|
| Operating margin negative; revenue −14% YoY, earnings −59% | Trading **below book** (0.75x P/B) and under 0.6x sales — asset-cheap |
| ROE under 2%; quality of earnings currently poor | Positive **FCF (~₹95 cr)** despite the profit trough |
| Quick ratio 0.57 — tight liquidity, inventory-heavy | Low leverage (D/E ~0.47x); balance sheet has room to weather the cycle |
| No visible dividend; income investors get nothing | Demerger/scheme of arrangement could unlock value in separable businesses |
| Restructuring adds uncertainty and noise | Low beta (0.56); idiosyncratic downside may be largely priced in at 56% off the high |

## What I'd want to confirm before any view
1. **Q4 FY26 line items** — open the press-release PDF [1] and the earnings transcript [3] for revenue, EBITDA margin, PAT, and segment split (pigments vs. agri-inputs vs. basic chemicals).
2. **The scheme of arrangement** — what exactly is being demerged/restructured, and into what entity. The NCLT meeting votes [4][5][6] are the key disclosure; the 30 Jun SEBI takeover filing [13] may signal a promoter-stake adjustment.
3. **Dividend history** — confirm via NSE/BSE corporate-action records whether MOL has paid any dividend in recent years (the feed shows none, but verify independently).
4. **Segment-level cyclicality** — is the −14% revenue / −59% earnings a pricing-driven chemical-cycle trough or a structural share loss?
